item.title: Houston Rockets beat Golden State Warriors in wild one that included Marcus Smart throwing a punch
item.description: Houston Rockets guard Amen Thompson (1) blocks Golden State Warriors forward Yaxel Lendeborg (1) shot in the first half of game action at the Toyota Center in Houston on Wednesday, Nov. 11, 2026. (Elizabeth Conley/Houston Chronicle) Even with Stephen Curry playing just six minutes before leaving with an injury, the Houston Rockets and Golden State Warriors played their usual chaotic battle. The Rockets survived against the short-handed Warriors with a 115-108 victory Wednesday at Toyota Center, but not before they lost Marcus Smart for throwing a punch at Charles Bassey. When the dust settled the Rockets (9-3) dealt the Warriors (8-4), who were on an eight-game winning streak, their first loss since Oct. 24. Amen Thompson had a huge third quarter for the Rockets, scoring 15 of his 19 points in the third. Kevin Durant led Houston with 20 points. Alperen Şengün finished an assist shy of a triple-double with 19 points, 13 rebounds and 9 assists. With Curry's scoring missing, Warriors rookie Yaxel Lendeborg finished with 25 points and 10 rebounds. Golden State coach Steve Kerr said Curry left the arena to get an MRI in the second half and they didn't know the severity of the injury yet, but added "concern is high." "He said he tweaked something in his abdominal area and that he's never done it before," Kerr said. Things got tense late in the third quarter, when Smart went face-to-face with the Warriors' big man during a dead ball. After the two exchanged words, Smart unleashed a right hand that appeared to graze Bassey's nose. Smart was ejected, but already had walked off the court and into the tunnel, knowing his fate. Rockets coach Ime Udoka said Smart didn't like how Bassey had wrapped up his elbow on the other end of the court, so he said something to him about it. "Bassey said, 'What you gonna do?'" Udoka said. "And he did it." Bassey made one of two free throws after the fracas to cut the Rockets' lead to 85-77. The Warriors showed further life early in the fourth quarter with Georges Niang and De'Anthony Melton hitting back-to-back 3-pointers to get within three points with nine minutes remaining. However, the Rockets scored eight straight, including two 3s by Reed Sheppard to stretch the lead back to double digits. item.title: City backs Para Athletics Worlds bid despite £6m warning
item.description: Didi Okoh won bronze at the 2024 Paralympics, and now hopes the World Para Athletics Championships will come to her home city [Press Association] Birmingham will bid to host the World Para Athletics Championships in 2029, despite warnings it could cost up to £6m to stage the event. The championships would be held at Alexander Stadium if the bid is successful, with the council describing it as an opportunity to build on the legacy of the 2022 Commonwealth Games. Paralympic sprinter, Ndidikama Okoh, said she was "so excited" at the prospect of the championships coming to Birmingham, where she began her journey in para athletics. But government-appointed commissioners overseeing the authority's financial recovery warned councillors that they should consider not bidding and assess whether the money could be better spent. The commissioners said the decision to bid was "conditional upon securing a minimum 50 per cent contribution from external partners". Jex Parkin, Leader of the Reform UK Group on Birmingham City Council, said: "It's an extremely prestigious and worthwhile event. But I do share the commissioners' queries regarding costs and priorities, particularly so soon after Birmingham hosted the 2022 Commonwealth Games." Deborah Harries, the Liberal Democrat cabinet member for culture, said councillors would be "rightly focused on affordability and risk", but said the event could generate "substantial" economic benefits. Okoh, who has lymphoedema , a condition which causes swelling, won bronze in the women's 100m T63 at both the Paris 2024 Paralympic Games and the 2025 World Para Athletics Championships. She moved to Birmingham about six years ago to study criminology and law at university and was inspired after watching para athletes compete at the 2022 Commonwealth Games. She said the city had "so much to offer" as a host for the championships. The championships would be hosted at Alexander Stadium [Local Democracy Reporting Service] "Birmingham did a really good job of hosting the Commonwealth Games, so it's nice to see that we're going to potentially get more opportunities," she said. "It's a really good opportunity to showcase what para athletes can do." Okoh said Birmingham's diverse communities helped make it a natural venue for an international event. "On that global scale, having people [visiting] from all across the world, if people are missing their home comforts, their home foods and stuff, you'll actually find it here," she said. She added that the city already had a large para sport community and said hosting the championships would have "a social impact as well". item.title: Houston Astros' Yordan Alvarez wins AL's Hank Aaron Award among accolades at MLB Awards
item.description: Astros slugger Yordan Alvarez, pictured with MLB Network's Siera Santos at Wednesday's awards show, took home the prestigious Hank Aaron Award as well as three other accolades on the eve of the MVP announcement. (Mary DeCicco/MLB Photos via Getty Images) LAS VEGAS - Yordan Alvarez was named the American League recipient of this year's Hank Aaron Award on Wednesday night in another nod to the Houston Astros slugger's prolific season. The Hank Aaron Award recognizes the top offensive performer in each league. Alvarez joins Jose Altuve as Astros players to win the award, which was introduced in 1999 to mark the 25th anniversary of Aaron breaking Babe Ruth's career home-run record. Altuve won the award in 2017 , the same year he was named the American League Most Valuable Player. Alvarez will learn Thursday whether he joins Altuve and Jeff Bagwell as Astros players to win a league MVP award. Alvarez garnered multiple honors at the MLB Awards show, which was held Wednesday night in Las Vegas with the slugger attending in person. Alvarez was also named AL Comeback Player of the Year, the Edgar Martinez Outstanding Designated Hitter and the All-MLB First Team designated hitter. Winners of the Hank Aaron Award were announced with Billye Aaron - the widow of Hank Aaron, who died in 2021 - among those on stage. Pete Crow-Armstrong of the Cubs was voted the National League winner. Alvarez delivered a brief comment on stage after he was named the AL winner. "It means a lot for me, especially because I wear the number 44," Alvarez said, referencing the number also worn by Aaron, at the awards event streamed by MLB.com. "I've been working really hard for this moment and it's really special for me to be part of and see my name on this trophy." To determine the Hank Aaron Award winners, a panel of 10 former winners and Hall of Famers vote on the list of 10 finalists from each league. Astros Hall of Famer Craig Biggio was part of this year's panel. Fans were allowed to vote from the list of finalists, as well. After playing in just 48 games in 2025 due to hand and ankle injuries, Alvarez this season led the majors in batting average (.316), on-base percentage (.432) and slugging percentage (.601), becoming the third Astros player to win a league batting title. Alvarez tied for second in the AL in home runs (42) and ranked second in runs batted in (106), recording career-high marks in both. He led the majors with 109 walks, including 33 intentional walks, and played in a career-high 158 games. Subscribe There’s more to Houston with the Chronicle. Subscribe today for just 25¢. item.title: Raptors’ record-tying feat wasted in loss to Celtics
item.description: Credit: Dan Hamilton-Imagn Images Raptors’ record-tying feat wasted in loss to Celtics appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Toronto Raptors came out of the gates firing in their Wednesday night clash against a Boston Celtics team that is on the second night of a back-to-back after coming off a spirited blowout victory over the Philadelphia 76ers. They scored 38 points in the first quarter, thanks in large part to a three-point barrage that tied a franchise record. According to Sportsnet Stats on X, the Raptors, by virtue of making 10 threes in the first quarter, tied the franchise record for most threes made in a single quarter. They went 10-of-18 from deep in the quarter, and that blistering start gave them a nine-point lead after 12 minutes of play. Toronto ended up with 16 made threes on the night on 43 attempts, which was good for a 37.2% clip. However, their offense sputtered for the rest of the game as the Celtics buckled down on defense. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The Raptors scored just 55 more points for the final three quarters, including just 32 in the second half, as the Celtics pulled away in crunch time with a 98-93 victory. Toronto still had a chance to win the game in the dying embers. After Jayson Tatum made two free throws to give Boston a one-point lead, 94-93, RJ Barrett would miss a go-ahead layup attempt. The Celtics would then get the defensive board, and Neemias Queta drilled two huge free throws to push their lead to three. The Raptors then failed to execute on an out of bounds play in an attempt to tie the game and force overtime. Jamison Battle would force a pass to Immanuel Quickley to the opposite side, and Sam Hauser intercepted the ball — sealing the defeat for Toronto. With Scottie Barnes and Kawhi Leonard both on the shelf , this was still a promising performance for the Raptors. Nonetheless, this latest defeat knocks them down to below .500 on the season (5-6), and they will be desperate to buy enough time for both of their star forwards to recover. item.title: Three Licking County volleyball players earn All-Ohio honors
item.description: Three of Licking County’s best volleyball players certainly measured up to the best in Ohio. Newark Catholic’s Leah Caudill and Sophia Basham and Granville’s Elle Mortimer recently received All-Ohio honors from the Ohio High School Volleyball Coaches Association. Caudill, a senior, was named to the Division VII first team. Caudill has recorded 376 kills, 296 digs and 83 blocks for the Green Wave, who have repeated as regional champions after winning the Division VI state championship last season. Basham, a junior, was named to the Division VII second team. Basham has recorded 330 kills, 231 digs and 111 blocks for the Green Wave. Mortimer, a senior, was named to the Division III second team. Mortimer recorded 353 kills, 171 digs and 105 blocks for the Blue Aces, who won a district championship. It might be the giant sombrero that the rugged lightweight wears to the ring, in keeping with his moniker of 'The Merthyr Mexican'. Or it will be the roaring lion prominently inked on his throat that invites the second glances and stares. Lately, though, the proud valleys fighter is showing there are more reasons for people to take note. Having already won British, Commonwealth and European titles, his upset of previously 16-fight unbeaten Khaleel Majid in May won him the WBA international belt at the weight above - and shot the 36-year-old up the rankings. Now, as he prepares to face Manchester's Zelfa Barrett for the WBA intercontinental lightweight title at Wembley Arena on Saturday, 14 November, Gwynne knows he has a chance to be known for more than a nickname and a neck tattoo. "I'm 36 but just feel like I'm getting better," Gwynne told BBC Sport Wales. "Just look at Anthony Cacace, he was 35 when he won his world title. That's what I want. item.title: Trusting Youth – It’s What Sunderland Does Best
item.description: SUNDERLAND, ENGLAND - NOVEMBER 08: Sunderland player Jules Ahoka applauds the fans after the Premier League 2026/27 match between Sunderland and Chelsea FC at Stadium of Light on November 08, 2026 in Sunderland, England. (Photo by Stu Forster/Getty Images) | Getty Images Jules Ahoka was handed his first Premier League appearance very early in the 1-0 win over Chelsea, being thrown into the mix with just minutes on the clock after Granit Xhaka went down injured. We’d seen a decent amount of him in other competitions, and few can argue that, either in Europe or the League Cup, he’d looked out of place despite barely playing any senior football before his move from Belgium in the summer. Ahoka came with a promising reputation, but there’s no doubting he was raw – and still is. However, the way he’s settled into the side is both a relief and exciting. There was a belief that he’d come in to be Xhaka’s understudy, and recent displays have left us feeling positive. If Ahoka is set to enjoy a breakthrough season in the Premier League, he’ll be another success story for Sunderland, proving it’s worth giving a youth player a first-team chance. Since Kyril Louis-Dreyfus took over, a recurring theme under the club’s head coaches has been trusting young players in the side. Some of these have been academy products, and although many have come and gone in the last few years, Chris Rigg is an example of a player who has been patient and earned his chance in the top flight and Europe. Timur Tutyerov, who joined the club as a teenager, has been trusted to lead the line on numerous occasions this season and has two goals to his name in six starts. It’s all about having faith in these players, and we’re seeing the rewards coming through with some top performances this season from the likes of Tutyerov and Ahoka. During the Championship promotion season, we were often told we didn’t have the experience to achieve anything and that our reliance on youth would be our downfall. This was followed by claims that we would struggle in the Premier League because we had too many young players without top-flight experience. As we reach the quarter-way mark of this third season of the RLB era, youth plays a key role in our team, whether that be through players we’ve signed from overseas or players produced and/or developed on Wearside. item.title: Australia captain Pat Cummins spotted in heated conversation with wife Becky in first public appearance since Khawaja’s Sandpaper claims
item.description: NEW DELHI: Australian cricket captain Pat Cummins has been spotted having what appeared to be a heated conversation with his wife, Becky, on a Sydney street. The incident marks his first public appearance since former Australian batter Usman Khawaja made fresh claims about the infamous 2018 ball-tampering scandal, also known as "Sandpaper-gate". According to footage published by The Australian on Wednesday, Cummins and Becky were seen having an animated discussion before heading inside a nearby property. Cummins, dressed casually in a T-shirt and shorts, appeared to remain relatively quiet during the exchange. The Australian captain is currently resting from the country's two white-ball series against England as he prepares for four upcoming Test matches against New Zealand. Fresh claims bring Sandpaper scandal back into focus The incident comes amid renewed controversy after Khawaja claimed that the entire Australian dressing room knew about the plan to tamper with the ball during the 2018 Test series in South Africa. Former opener David Warner, who was also involved in the scandal, has supported Khawaja's claims. In his autobiography Sabr, released on Tuesday, Khawaja shared his account of the events that resulted in Cricket Australia suspending Steve Smith, David Warner and Cameron Bancroft. When asked about the possibility of Khawaja revealing details that differed from the findings of the official investigation, Cummins had earlier said: “It’s obviously a long time ago. All the investigations, everything was done back then. Answered every question a million times,” Cummins said. “It was dealt with then, all I can say is as a group we’ve moved on. Very happy with the last eight or nine years, how we’ve been as a group and evolved. He didn’t go into too much detail . . . As always it was ‘no worries, you can tell your story, that’s fine’.” Khawaja refuses to reveal more details Khawaja has since cancelled his remaining media appearances for the book after facing tough questions on ABC's 7.30 program. During the interview, he was asked whether he was upset that the bowlers had not admitted knowing about the plan to rough up the ball using sandpaper. “I’ll say again, I’ve given my statement about what happened the game before,” Khawaja said. “I was very open and honest to what I saw and what conversations I had. Sometimes I’m very specific on things, and sometimes I’m a bit vague on things, and I do it on purpose because I’m trying to tell a story.” When questioned further about the bowlers' involvement, he refused to comment. “I’m just not going … I’m not going to entertain that,” Khawaja said. “I’m not going to really speak on any more of it at this moment.”

item.title: OTD (12/11/1983) Making Plans For Nigel: Sunderland Take The Sting Out Of The Hornets
item.description: Alan Durban’s third – and, as it would turn out, final – season at Sunderland had picked up after a slow start that saw the club with just one win in the first six Division One games. A 1-0 victory over Bob Paisley’s Liverpool at Anfield in October, and a 2-1 win against Arsenal at Highbury, had certainly shown that the team was no pushover, and had higher aspirations than finishing just three points clear of the relegation zone, as they had done the previous campaign. After the trip to Highbury, Sunderland had faced a midweek Milk Cup trip to Norwich – a nil-nil scoreline drawing the ire of Canaries striker Mick Channon, who said: “We would never go away and play like they did. In fact, I’m glad we don’t play like that otherwise Mick Channon would have retired by now.” I’m glad I don’t refer to myself in the third person, Mick. That meant a Roker replay would soon follow – but in the meantime the lads were looking to build on the three points in North London with another three at home to Watford. It would be no small ask. Watford, under the headline-grabbing stewardship of Elton John, and the exceptionally promising managerial ability of Graham Taylor, had finished second in the First Division the season before. 1982/83 had been their first season ever in the top flight, with Taylor guiding them quickly up the leagues since taking over the Fourth Division club in 1977. For Sunderland, progress had been rather more sedate. While Durban – who’d taken over the permanent reins from Ken Knighton in the summer of 1981 – had been stifled by a lack of funds to really take the team forward at pace, he’d built a smart, young squad that, while capable of producing some excellent displays was also, predictable, a little inconsistent. Progress is rarely linear, yet the feeling was the team was heading steadily in the right direction. item.description: Man United to go all out to land Malo Gusto, Mauricio Pochettino loves him Manchester United are reeling in 18th place in the Premier League after 10 games, with head coach Michael Carrick on the brink of the sack. There are valid reasons for INEOS to pull the plug, but the co-owners are not devoid of blame either, having failed to strengthen at the back despite the glaring need for reinforcements. Full-back is an area where the Red Devils have struggled, with left-back Luke Shaw perennially injured as expected while right-back Diogo Dalot has struggled to plug the gap in the Englishman’s absence. According to recent reports, the 20-time English league champions have identified Mauricio Pochettino, the United States men’s national team head coach, as the replacement for the former United midfielder . Why United need new full-backs Interestingly, the Argentine coach is known for his high-octane style of play, in which he likes to push his full-backs high and wide. United lack the quality needed to pull this off, which explains why the club are looking at Chelsea right-back Malo Gusto ahead of the January window. The Frenchman enjoyed his most productive spell under the USMNT boss during the 2023/24 season, notching nine assists in all competitions for Chelsea, his most productive season for the Blues to date. talkSPORT has reported that Manchester City are also eyeing the France international due to Enzo Maresca’s close ties with the right-back. With Malo Gusto managing only three starts in the league this season, a change in scenery could do his career a world of good. M. Chelsea value the Frenchman at £75million. “The Chelsea defender has seen his role reduced since Xabi Alonso’s arrival at Stamford Bridge, leading him to be linked with an exit.” Malo Gusto can also play on the opposite flank and can double up as a defensive midfielder or even a wing-back if needed. Such versatility would be an asset for Pochettino. However, a move for the Blues ace could spell trouble for Dalot. With City reportedly facing a hefty punishment for breaching financial rules, United could potentially have a free run at the player. But such an outlay could prove difficult to pull off for INEOS.

ANAHEIM, Calif. – For so many recent nights, so much had gone the way of the Anaheim Ducks with eight straight games of five or more goals. However, on some nights, it just doesn’t bounce your way at all. Riding their own five-game winning streak, the Nashville Predators finished opportunities where the Ducks simply did not in the face of a stout goaltending performance from Justus Annunen in a 4-2 Nashville win on Wednesday at Honda Center. Anaheim (9-8-1, 19 points) snaps its five-game winning streak and its white hot offensive run, while Nashville pushed out to its sixth straight win. Cutter Gauthier continued his ludicrous goal-scoring streak, as the puck found him in the first period for his seventh straight game with a strike and his 14th goal in that span. Gauthier tied Corey Perry (2013-14) for the third-longest streak in team history. Teemu Selanne owns the two longest streaks at eight games (1998-99) and 11 games (1997-98). Mikael Granlund pulled the Ducks back within one late in the third period, 3-2, on a one-timer from Beckett Sennecke, who made up for his second missed breakaway with the feed. Jayden Struble evened it up for the Predators in the first period, as he pushed forward into open space where Travis Mitchell and Tristan Luneau jumped up into the play and couldn’t break it up. Nashville went ahead late in the second period, when Nils Höglander ripped off a highlight reel stunner, 2-1. Jackson LaCombe vacated the front of the net to make a play, but it went behind him to Höglander, who went between his legs and top shelf for the finish. It was a two-goal lead for Nashville midway through the third period, even if no one knew it immediately. Anaheim couldn’t clear the zone, and newly acquired Shane Wright found a rebound in the slot and shot it off the center post in the back of the net. The puck came out so quickly, no one immediately registered it as a goal, but on review, it was all the way in, 3-1. item.description: Ilia Topuria could get a chance to recreate one of the most infamous moments in MMA history. As fans know by now, Merab Dvalishvili was caught in a sneak attack involving Usman Nurmagomedov and his Dagestani entourage in a hotel lobby in Abu Dhabi. Footage of the altercation showed Dvalishvili in the middle of an interview when Nurmagomedov approached him from behind and slapped him. Things quickly escalated into an all-out brawl , with Dvalishvili’s friend, Saba Lazishvili, jumping in and taking down two Dagestani fighters. The incident drew widespread criticism from the MMA community, particularly from Topuria , who called Nurmagomedov and his men cowards and claimed that the undefeated PFL fighter had been detained. Even Conor McGregor joined the conversation, although his reaction took a rather different turn. The Irishman shared a morphed image referencing his infamous UFC 223 bus attack on Khabib Nurmagomedov and his team, with Topuria’s head edited onto his body. The image showed McGregor throwing a dolly at the bus eight years ago, only this time with Topuria in his place. After learning about the confrontation, McGregor flew from Ireland to New York on a private jet with his entourage to confront Nurmagomedov. Although the Dagestani fighter escaped unharmed inside the vehicle, the shattered glass and flying debris caused significant collateral damage. The incident also had major consequences for UFC 223, with three fights being scrapped. Michael Chiesa vs. Anthony Pettis and Ray Borg vs. Brandon Moreno were canceled, while Lobov was pulled from his scheduled bout against Alex Caceres by the UFC because of his involvement in the arena attack alongside McGregor. item.title: Boston Celtics 10-2 start has promising connection
item.description: The Boston Celtics have put together a lot of great seasons in the last decade, but none surpass the 2023-24 campaign, which culminated in a championship. Before Boston captured the Larry O'Brien Championship Trophy that June, it jumped out to a 10-2 start during the regular season. The C's are off to the exact same start three years later, albeit with a very different roster. After coming back from a 22-point deficit on Wednesday night to defeat the Toronto Raptors , 98-93, in Canada, the Celtics are 10-2 overall and on their second five-game winning streak of the young season. This marks their best record through 12 contests since the aforementioned title campaign, as the Green Team posted records of 9-3 and 5-7 within that same number of games during the 2024-25 and 2025-26 seasons, respectively. Now, this impressive coincidence doesn't mean the Celtics are championship-bound. The 2023-24 squad was utterly dominant and featured multiple All-Stars who are no longer with the Green Team, including Jaylen Brown, Jrue Holiday, Kristaps Porzingis, and Al Horford. Celtics star Jayson Tatum remains, though, and he has fellow 2024 NBA champion Derrick White at his side in the starting lineup along with a valuable addition: nine-time All-Star and first-year Celtic Paul George. The new-look C's might not measure up to the Banner 18 Celtics, yet they're churning out wins all the same. That's in part because the 2026-27 Celtics, like many Green Teams of old, emphasize the importance of every game — no matter its magnitude. Wednesday was the perfect example of this mentality. The Celtics are 5-0 at home this season. That's their best start at TD Garden since the 2023-24 campaign. pic.twitter.com/SKBHzIXL5I — Daniel Donabedian (@danield1214) November 5, 2026 The Celtics could've quit on the second night of a back-to-back once they trailed a banged-up Raptors team by double digits. A quicker loss would mean a quicker journey home following a four-game road trip. However, instead of taking it easy, the C's rallied in the second half and stole a road win up north. "Tenth year in the league, (I'm) understanding the emotional roller coaster of the NBA season, and just kind of putting things in perspective," Tatum said on Tuesday night after the Celtics routed the Philadelphia 76ers in a primetime matchup. "They all count as one." While the current Eastern Conference-leading Celtics still have a lot of work to do before they can reach the highs of the 2023-24 crew, their first steps have been in the right direction. They'll aim to stay on the winning path on Sunday evening, when they host the 7-4 Dallas Mavericks at TD Garden.
